findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Inspector observed a few dairy food items being store on the floor in the dairy walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware and PIC immediately remove the items and stored them appropriately. Ensure that food items stored at least 6 inches from the floor to protect them from splash, dust, and other contaminants. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the banana room to be holding a variety of perishable foods. The banana room holds around 55F. The food when temped was between 48F and 55F. The manager, staff and I worked to remove TCS foods.The facility used their scanner to facilitate the throw away process. A copy of the list was provided to the inspector. Items were removed to the dumpster. The violation is considered corrected at the time of inspection. Do not store food that requires refrigeration temperatures in the banana room. One employee stated that they used to move food in and out of the banana room to the cold room every 3 hours. Do not use this process of letting food come out of temperature by rotating food in and out of the properly refrigerated holding room.  

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.11: FROZEN FOOD  Stored frozen foods shall be maintained frozen.

Complaint is valid. Whole frozen turkeys in the open top freezer case are observed to have areas where meat was soft to the touch. The unit is functioning properly. The issue is from portions of the turkeys sticking up above the freeze line for too long. Turkeys in the case were evaluated for soft spots. Turkeys with areas that had thawed were removed from the case. According to management, these turkeys will be discarded after they are scanned out. There were 8 turkeys all together. They were 22.51, 13.96, 23.58, 22.84, 22.74, 13.97, 12.94 and 23.30 pounds respectively. The total weight of turkey discarded was 155.84 lbs. Management chose to discard out of an abundance of caution. It is difficult to keep odd shaped items below the freeze line in open top units. Watch cases like this regularly throughout the day as customer shopping can also move items above the freeze line and cause the items to thaw.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Italian sausage is observed at 48F. Air temp was 60F according to thermometer. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times. (41°F or below, or 135°F or above) The case it was in is over stocked and was in defrost at 3pm.  The items were discarded in the garbage.  Watch the case closely when it goes into defrost again. Suggest having the case evaluated.  The case cae back into temperature as soon as the defrost went off. 
11, 1 lb 3oz packages, were discarded in the garbage.

findings.comment: In seafood observed a sleeve of back trays on the floor along with a box containing boxes of gloves. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law. Store single use items properly.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: The facility in back stock/storage has some areas where debris is collecting. These include but may not be limited to:1)  the area around returns and either side of bank of cabinets, 2) the area under a cabinet where the kick plate is broken or missing 3) areas on either side of garage doors for docks. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors. Make sure to maintain floors free of accumulated soil and debris especially items which could be utilized as bedding or harborage for rodents.

findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed mutliple dented cans throughout the soup/canned good isle. Management noted staff checks for dented cans nightly. Canned goods were inspected and any dented cans were removed to return for credit.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 1) Yogurt and sour cream display cases have plasitc bags under food to prevent debris falling through grates. These bags are soiled. Management noted the bags are supposed to be stored under the grates to catch debris. Make sure these bags are switched out regularly as any debris accumulation occurs. 2) Observed multiple gaps around the mop sink. Caulk all gaps around the mop sink and gaps in corner of the wall to make for a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.
